summary.headline: Chola Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 22% YoY to INR29,612 crore and AUM 23% to INR2,54,392 crore, with net credit cost down to 1.5% from 1.8%.
summary.overview: Cholamandalam reported Q1 FY27 aggregate disbursements of INR29,612 crore (up 22% YoY) and AUM of INR2,54,392 crore (up 23%). Net credit cost fell to 1.5% from 1.8% a year ago, NIM rose 42 bps YoY and ROA reached 3.7% versus 3.1%. Gross Stage 3 rose QoQ seasonally (about 25 bps, per management), and the company changed its disbursement recognition to cheque debit date, which depresses reported disbursement growth this quarter. Management reiterated 22-23% growth and 1.5% credit cost guidance for FY27, and kept the INR200 crore management overlay intact.

financial_highlights.value: AUM growth 26% YoY; LAP AUM INR54,130 crore (+23% YoY)

financial_highlights.change: from 1.8% a year ago (-24 bps YoY per CEO/Chairman)
from 3.84% in March 2026; 3.52% to 3.89% same period last year

segments.name: Vehicle finance (Auto)
segments.commentary: Disbursements grew about 21% YoY and AUM 19% to INR1,24,132 crore; used and new vehicle disbursements each grew over 20% on a like-for-like basis. Stage 3 rose to 4.05% from 3.84% in March 2026.

segments.name: MSME (LAP, SME, SBPL)
segments.commentary: MSME disbursements grew 6% YoY while AUM grew 26%; LAP AUM INR54,130 crore (+23%), SME AUM INR9,923 crore (+39%), SBPL AUM INR3,730 crore (+40%). LAP credit loss was about 37 bps in Q1 versus about 30 bps guided; SBPL NCL 2.3%, pretax ROA 7.9%.

segments.name: Consumer (home loans, CSEL, gold)
segments.commentary: Consumer disbursements rose 52% YoY; home loan AUM INR23,644 crore (+22%), CSEL AUM INR15,884 crore (+12%) with CSEL pretax ROA 3.3% and credit cost down from 6.7% to 4.7%, gold loan AUM INR2,143 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 net credit cost guidance of about 1.5% was described as achieved in Q1 itself; management expects credit cost to improve further from here.
Management says 22-23% disbursement and AUM growth remains achievable; Q2 expected to be as good as or better than Q1, with Q3-Q4 facing a high base.
Cost of funds expected to rise about 10 bps in H2 on an assumed 25-50 bps repo hike, but full-year cost of funds expected flat versus FY26 as a percentage of average assets.
NIM expected to improve, supported by CV and gold mix; management says 3.5% pretax ROA is a minimum target.
INR430 crore of remaining CCDs expected to convert into equity in October 2026.
Gold loan: 360 new branches planned in FY27, AUM from over INR2,000 crore toward INR5,000 crore in FY27; per-branch AUM INR12-15 crore; new branches expected to be profitable by next year-end.
About 125 vehicle finance resident locations to be converted into full-fledged branches by end of FY27.
capex_capacity: Gold loan network to expand by 360 branches this year; LAP, affordable housing and home loans to open 100-plus branches a year, per management.
Vehicle finance has 600-plus resident locations; about 125 to be converted into full branches by year-end.
Collections team of about 30,000 people; CSEL collections 55% digital.
demand_pricing: Management says all business lines, including VF, LAP, housing, SME, SBPL, CSEL, gold and consumer durables, were trending well in July 2026 with no adverse impact seen yet.

Disbursement recognition changed from cheque handover to cheque debit into the customer or dealer account from Q1 FY27; management says like-for-like growth remains above 20% in LAP, HL and used vehicles, and the change reverses from Q2.
Home loan yields reportedly up YoY (interest income 15.9% of assets vs 15.5% last year); Q-o-Q yield dip attributed to seasonal collection-income pattern.
CSEL approval rate about 35-40% for business loans and about 60% for salaried loans; FEMI around 3% for 15 months.
Gold loan yields on par with or slightly above peers, roughly 16-17%; about 90% of gold customers are new to Chola, with 20-25% new to gold loans.
Management noted MSME and SBPL disbursement growth of 30%+ at SBPL as a structural high-yield business.

qa_highlights.question: Stage 3 rising QoQ in most segments; is there risk to the 1.5% credit cost guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said net credit cost already fell to 1.5% from 1.8%; GNPA rose only 25 bps QoQ versus a larger seasonal rise last year. No visibility yet on Q3 stress from monsoon or geopolitics; rainfall forecast is 92% of average.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LAP and vehicle finance Stage 3 rise YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP credit loss was 37 bps in Q1 vs 30 bps guided, with Stage 3 at 2.3-2.5%, which management called stable. VF Stage 3 rose 20 bps QoQ to 4.05%, versus 45 bps QoQ last year.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of funds outlook and rate hike assumption?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds may rise about 10 bps in H2, assuming a 25-50 bps repo hike; full-year cost of funds flat YoY. About 25-30% of bank borrowing is MCLR-linked (1-3 month MCLR, no premium); bonds are fixed rate and currently costlier than bank funds.

qa_highlights.question: Is the SBPL NPA rise a concern and can CSEL exceed group ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: SBPL NCL is 2.3% with pretax ROA of 7.9%; Stage 3 depends on ARC sales, and a sale was done in Q4 and is planned for next quarter. CSEL pretax ROA is 3.3% with credit cost down to 4.7%, and management expects it to exceed the group ROA soon.

qa_highlights.question: Can PBT-ROTA exceed 3.5% by Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3.5% is a minimum target; credit cost can fall further and cost of funds gains may partly reverse, so no number was given beyond holding or improving it. CCD conversion is small (about INR630 crore) and not a game changer, per CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the IRDAI insurance circular on income?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO declined to quantify; said the circular is not expected to apply in FY27 and the impact is unknown until issued.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR200 crore management overlay remain intact and have PD/LGD changed?
qa_highlights.answer: The overlay is fully intact and will be reviewed at year-end. PCR dipped because 100% provided VF cases were written off (average provisioning about 48%). PD/LGD are reviewed annually, now in the December quarter.

risks_watch: Seasonal Stage 3 rise and below-average monsoon (92% forecast) could lift Q3-Q4 credit costs; management flagged El Nino, the West Asia conflict and tariffs as risks.
H2 cost of funds: a 25-50 bps repo hike could push up borrowing costs; FY27 flat cost-of-funds guidance is contingent on this.
Growth base effect in Q3-Q4 as FY26 growth accelerated only from H2; disbursement recognition change distorts QoQ comparisons until Q2.
Pending IRDAI insurance circular may affect income; impact not quantified.
ALM mismatch: analyst cited about 10% negative mismatch in the FY26 annual report; management said the investor-deck cumulative gap shows no negative mismatch, to be followed up offline.
Gold loan ramp: 360 new branches and per-branch targets; yields 16-17%; new branches expected to reach profitability by next year-end.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and asset quality, with management repeatedly saying the 1.5% credit cost target was already achieved in Q1. It was more cautious on H2 (rate hikes, El Nino, geopolitics), declining to predict beyond one or two quarters, and it declined to quantify the IRDAI circular impact.

Our delinquency level is only 6%. That means 94% are current.
